Before any full-length measurements, it was found that Windows MSVC contains cl.exe, but not standard headlines/library C++. Errors in environment preparation and CMake saved; solvers were not started. Global installation Visual Studio It doesn't change.

Diagnostic control and timer assembly are carried out in the already available Ubuntu-24.04 WSL (GCC 13.3, CMake 3.28). Same source. To match what's missing in MSVC __uint128 F4-branch is compiled by force with Z3_FF_HAS_UINT128=0. It's a characteristic of the diagnostic assembly, not a change in formulas/times Linux cannot be directly attributed to the established Windows DLL: The final comparison of acceleration parameters is performed on the unchanged set Windows DLL.

Temporary object compilation files are in /tmp/seq27-430d19e-20261106; The original archive, patch, commands, logs, and finite libraries are saved in the new series. The original series is the same. Small benchmarks pass before profiling; library construction and measurable search are not performed simultaneously.
